title: SSE: interleaved function-call frame boundaries, resumable replay, and graceful fallback
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: Streaming responses that mix freeform token streams with embedded function-call frames and structured JSON blocks are brittle across reconnects and heterogeneous clients. Existing resume tokens only represent byte offsets and do not guarantee that a partially-emitted function-call or JSON object will be reassembled safely on reconnect, which leads to either duplicate function invocations or malformed structured outputs shown to callers.

Goal: Implement a backward-compatible SSE framing/handshake extension and server-side replay strategy that: 1) marks function-call and structured-output boundaries in the stream, 2) surfaces minimal resume metadata that clients can use to request a safe replay window, and 3) provides a graceful fallback for older clients (legacy SSE or eventstream consumers) without requiring immediate client changes.

Constraints and non-goals: We must not break existing hosted API behavior for customers on pinned SDK versions. This change must be opt-in via a negotiated handshake header for Dedicated/Private customers during rollout. We cannot require a full protocol version bump for all clients. Non-goal: designing a completely new wire format — we will extend SSE events and reuse the existing resume token concept with additional stable tokens.

Acceptance criteria: 
- New SSE control events emitted for boundary markers (frame_start/frame_end, function_call_complete) documented and tested.
- Resume token augmented to include sequence-id and last-complete-call-id; server can reply to a resume request with pre-seek and replay window.
- Old clients continue to work unchanged (receive the same token stream) but are not guaranteed partial-function-call replay correctness; we provide guidance in release notes.
- Integration tests that simulate disconnects at: mid-token, mid-json-object, and mid-function-call; after reconnect, client-state reconstructs to the same semantic output (no duplicate function invocations, no truncated JSON).
- Rollout plan and canary metrics defined in console dashboard (replay success, duplicate-function-rate, format-errors).

Design summary: 
- Control events: emit event: ctl with JSON body {"t":"boundary","seq":<int>,"kind":"frame|json|func","call_id":<optional>} when a semantic boundary is reached. These ctl events are single-line SSE events; legacy clients will ignore unknown event types (SSE ignores unknown event names) so compatibility is preserved.
- Resume metadata: resume-token -> base64("seq:<n>;offset:<byte>;last_call:<call_id>"). On reconnect client supplies resume-token and desired replay-policy header (replay=trim|replay=full). Server validates and decides a safe seek point: if last_call in token is complete, seek to offset; if incomplete, seek back to prior frame boundary.
- Idempotency for function-calls: server attaches stable call_id to each function call emission and records call outcomes for short TTL (configurable per deployment). If replay includes a previously completed call_id, server replies with a no-op marker to avoid duplicate side-effecting replays.
- Structured-output validation: server emits small per-object checksums as ctl events to help clients validate reassembly. Clients that opt-in will verify checksum after reassembly and request a full replay if mismatch.

Implementation notes: 
- Server: streaming runtime will lift boundary detection into tokenizer layer to avoid extra passes. ctl events are generated when token stream boundary heuristics detect a completed JSON object or function call.
- Handshake: new request header X-Redwood-Stream-Proto: v1.1; if present, server enables ctl events and resume-token augmentation. If absent, server behaves as today.
- Backpressure & ordering: ctl events are emitted inline and count toward token budget but are small; ensure batching preserves ordering between data and ctl events.

Telemetry and observability: add metrics: stream.replay.attempts, stream.replay.success, stream.duplicate_function_invocations, stream.checksum_mismatches. Add Console dashboard rows for canary.

Rollout: start with Dedicated customers on runtime-1.22 as opt-in. After 4 weeks and no regression, flip for hosted-canary. Provide SDK patch for client-side resume parsing and connector examples for Node/Python.

Risk: Older proxies and HTTP streaming intermediaries that strip unknown SSE event names are rare but possible; we will document fallback: use an alternate content-type negotiation endpoint for those environments.
comments: 2025-02-15 - Ava Patel: Created ticket after failure postmortem where a reconnect caused duplicated webhook-side effects due to incomplete function-call replay. Attached initial design sketch.

2025-02-18 - Miguel Santos: Spiked on tokenizer-layer hooks; confirming we can generate boundary ctl events with <2% CPU overhead in microbench. Added simple timeline for implementation: generator -> handshake -> idempotency-store TTL -> end-to-end tests.

2025-02-20 - Design review (Kara Liu): Suggested using existing SSE 'event' field for ctl rather than inventing a binary prefix; aligns with browser eventsource semantics. Also requested API docs update and migration guide.

2025-02-25 - Security review (initial): No secrets added; risk matrix OK. Note: idempotency store access must be authenticated in Private deployments — will follow standard KMS keys for on-prem components.

2025-02-28 - QA (Ravi Menon): Added test cases simulating disconnect at: mid-token, inside JSON object, before function-call end. Found an edge case where partial control-event arrives after reconnect; fixed by ensuring ctl events are emitted with finalizing marker 'frame_end' before socket close.

2025-03-03 - Miguel Santos: Implemented server-side ctl emission and basic resume-token encode/decode. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4098. Integration tests starting in CI; asking for review from infra and SDK owners.
2025-03-03 - Ava Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to include telemetry and rollout steps.
